ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As illustrated, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $AB=10\,\text{cm}$, $BC=8\,\text{cm}$. Point $D$ is on side $AB$ with $AD=AC$, $AE\perp CD$ at foot $E$. Point $F$ is the midpoint of $BC$. Then, what is the length of $EF$ in $\text{cm}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: In $\triangle ABC$, where $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $AB=10\text{cm}$, $BC=8\text{cm}$,\\
we have $AC=\sqrt{AB^{2}-BC^{2}}=\sqrt{10^{2}-8^{2}}=6\text{cm}$.\\
Thus, $AD=AC=6\text{cm}$,\\
and $BD=AB-AD=10-6=4\text{cm}$.\\
Since $AD=AC$ and $AE\perp CD$,\\
it follows that $CE=DE$, meaning point $E$ is the midpoint of $CD$,\\
and given that point $F$ is the midpoint of $BC$,\\
$EF$ serves as the midsegment of $\triangle CBD$,\\
thus $EF=\frac{1}{2}BD=\boxed{2}\text{cm}$.

Because AE is perpendicular to CD, the altitude from the apex A to the base CD also bisects CD, so E is the midpoint of CD. The text states that F is the midpoint of BC. Therefore, in triangle CBD, E and F are the midpoints of CD and CB respectively. Thus EF is a midsegment of triangle CBD, so EF = BD/2 = 4/2 = 2 cm.
